label: Kahler Forms
notes: This lecture sits at the meeting point of symplectic, complex, and Riemannian geometry. A Kahler form is a symplectic form that respects an integrable complex structure. Stress at the outset that the whole subject is governed by one matrix of Hermitian coefficients being positive definite, which is the engine for every later result.

label: Three Geometries Agree
notes: Open by reminding students that a complex structure plus a compatible symplectic form already builds a Riemannian metric. Kahler is the case where all three structures are simultaneously parallel. The novelty over almost complex compatibility is integrability of J, which lets us use holomorphic coordinates and Dolbeault calculus.

label: Type Decomposition
notes: Walk through how the eigenspaces of J split forms into bidegrees. Compatibility kills the pure holomorphic and antiholomorphic parts, leaving only the mixed type. Emphasize that this type decomposition is the algebraic skeleton on which closedness and positivity will be imposed in the next slides.

label: The Kahler Condition
notes: State the definition crisply: a Kahler form is a closed, real, positive form of type one-one. Give the five gates from the notebook checklist and point out that each gate is independently testable on the coefficient matrix. Closedness here is the genuinely restrictive condition, separating Kahler from merely Hermitian.

label: Positivity and the Hermitian Matrix
notes: Tie positivity of the form to positive definiteness of the Hermitian matrix h. Explain that the associated metric is the real part and the form is the imaginary part. Nondegeneracy is just the determinant being nonzero, and positivity strengthens this so the metric is genuinely Riemannian.

label: The Local Kahler Potential
notes: This is the construction machine of the theory. A strictly plurisubharmonic real function rho yields a Kahler form by applying i partial partial-bar. Because partial squared and partial-bar squared vanish, the form is automatically closed. Stress the converse: locally every Kahler form arises this way, by Dolbeault triviality.

label: Potentials in Action
notes: Compare the flat potential, whose complex Hessian is constant, with the Fubini-Study potential, whose Hessian bends the density. The contour pictures make the difference visible. The point is that the eigenvalues of the complex Hessian are exactly the positivity certificate for the resulting two-form.

label: Fubini-Study on CP^n
notes: Introduce the model compact Kahler manifold. The potential log of one plus norm squared gives a globally defined form despite being only a local potential, because chart transitions add pluriharmonic terms that i partial partial-bar annihilates. This well-definedness is the subtle heart of the projective example.

label: CP^1 is the Round Sphere
notes: Ground the abstraction in the simplest case. On the one chart of CP^1 the Fubini-Study density is one over one plus r squared, all squared, and integrating it gives finite total area pi. This is the round area form on the two-sphere up to scale, the most familiar Kahler manifold of all.

label: Submanifolds and Projective Varieties
notes: Close the logical loop. Restricting a strictly plurisubharmonic potential to a complex submanifold takes a principal minor of a positive matrix, which stays positive. Hence complex submanifolds of Kahler manifolds are Kahler, and nonsingular projective varieties inherit Kahler structure from the Fubini-Study form on the ambient projective space.

label: Recap
notes: Recap the chain of ideas: type one-one, closed, real, positive, then potentials, then Fubini-Study, then submanifolds. Send students to the notebook exploration prompt about varying the coefficient in a logarithmic potential and predicting when positivity survives, which rehearses the Hessian test directly.
